text: The S&P 500 fell 1.03% to 7,340.53, its lowest close since late July, and the Dow lost 848.75 points as software and other tech names led the drop.
Nvidia reported about $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue and guided to about $130 billion next quarter, both above forecasts; its shares rose in after-hours trading.
The VIX rose 11% to 25.46 after touching 27.73 during the day, its highest close of the recent selloff.
Gold eased about $7 to near $3,849, while silver rose 0.8% to about $47.36, nudging the gold/silver ratio down to about 81.3 from 82.3.
Gold miners and silver funds edged higher: GDX rose 0.8% to $79.57 and SLV 0.6% to $42.64.
Treasury yields slipped about 2 bp, with the 10-year at 5.10% and the 2-year at 4.80%.
Bitcoin fell about 2% to roughly $63,500 as rising Fed hike expectations weighed on riskier assets.
Brent crude rose roughly 0.6–0.8% to about $93 after reported tanker attacks near the Strait of Hormuz, though worries about too much supply persist.
